bull.b: Sustained, accelerating free cash flow provides durable funding for R&D, product ramps, and capital allocation without adding leverage. That cash conversion supports multi‑year AI/data center investment, cushions cyclical downturns, and increases strategic optionality for capacity or M&A.

bull.t: Rapid Data Center / AI revenue growth
bull.b: A structural surge in Data Center and AI demand is driving double‑digit, sustainable revenue expansion and share gains for EPYC and Instinct. Strong enterprise and hyperscaler partnerships plus an expanding AI product roadmap underpin a lasting TAM expansion and recurring server traction.

bull.t: Conservative leverage and balance sheet flexibility
bull.b: Very low leverage gives the company resilience through cycles and the ability to fund H2 product ramps, R&D, and go‑to‑market investment. Conservative capital structure reduces refinancing risk and supports multi‑year strategic initiatives without materially constraining cash deployment.

bear.t: Gross margin dilution risk from GPU ramp
bear.b: Scaling lower‑margin Instinct GPU products can meaningfully dilute consolidated gross margins as AI accelerators gain share, pressuring sustainable profitability metrics. This tradeoff could limit margin expansion even as revenue grows, and complicate long‑term margin guidance.

Rapidly rising R&D and go‑to‑market spend raises the fixed cost base and increases earnings volatility if revenue growth misses expectations. Higher, less-predictable OpEx reduces operating leverage and makes medium‑term profitability and cash conversion more sensitive to execution.

External foundry capacity, component supply and data center power/build‑out limits pose structural constraints on the company’s ability to scale multi‑GW AI deployments quickly. These bottlenecks can cap revenue realization timing and increase execution risk despite strong demand.
